headword: {魏志倭人伝|ぎしわじんでん}
gloss: the Gishi Wajinden (Chinese account of early Japan)

definitions.gloss: the Gishi Wajinden, the account of the Wa in the Chinese Records of the Three Kingdoms
definitions.explanation: The conventional Japanese name for the section on the Wa people (early Japan) in the Book of Wei of the Chinese history Records of the Three Kingdoms, compiled in the late third century. It is the oldest substantial description of Japan and the source for Himiko and Yamatai.

examples.japanese: {魏志倭人伝|ぎしわじんでん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{卑弥呼|ひみこ}→卑弥呼：31978_himiko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名|な}→名：03496_na⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: The name Himiko appears in the Gishi Wajinden.

examples.japanese: ⟦{邪馬台国|やまたいこく}→邪馬台国：33242_yamataikoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{魏志倭人伝|ぎしわじんでん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{記述|きじゅつ}→記述：05819_kijutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧もと⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{議論|ぎろん}→議論：02650_giron⟧⟦されて→する：00392_suru⟧きた。
examples.english: The location of Yamatai has long been debated on the basis of the Gishi Wajinden's account.

examples.japanese: {三世紀|さんせいき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{様子|ようす}→様子：01521_yousu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{伝|つた}える→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧{魏志倭人伝|ぎしわじんでん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{中国|ちゅうごく}→中国：28300_chuugoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{歴史書|れきししょ}『{三国志|さんごくし}』⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一部|いちぶ}→一部：06783_ichibu⟧だ。
examples.english: The Gishi Wajinden, which describes Japan in the third century, is part of the Chinese history Records of the Three Kingdoms.

notes:
The name is a label, not a book title: {魏志|ぎし} is the Book of Wei, {倭人|わじん} the people of Wa (the old Chinese name for Japan), and {伝|でん} an account. Learners meet it in school history, as the earliest detailed account of Japan (shorter mentions of Wa appear in older Chinese histories such as the Book of Han).
